newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Weather, demand pushes wheat higher.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Weather, demand pushes wheat higher.

text.p: The Australian wheat market continues to be weather-driven with wheat prices over the past week rising by A$3.00 a tonne, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.
The market was led by the stock feed market with dairy demand noticeably strong, it said.
With rain still required in some areas across New South Wales and the Mallee region in Victoria, stocks are still being held on farm, pushing up prices for high protein wheat.
This trend should discontinue once a full rain break comes through, it said.
Latest Week Year to Date Previous Year
The AWB's fob pool price for Australian Standard White wheat remained unchanged at A$203.00 a tonne, it said.

On the international market, the USDA report on the 1997/98 wheat balance sheet pushed U.S. wheat futures sharply lower even though the supply/demand report was generally regarded as neutral to bearish for the market, AWB said.
The USDA balance sheet showed a significant and unexpected increase in world wheat ending stocks which pressured prices.
A stronger U.S.futures market on Friday was primarily in reaction to reports of large old crop sales. Talk of leaf rust also contributed, it said.
